value_stream.name: Corporate Real Estate & Property Portfolio Management

fields.Participants: Lease Admin Mgr, Director, Facilities & Real Estate, Finance/Transfer Pricing (links to VS-72), Legal, Tax (links to VS-79)
fields.Trigger: New property added (W3187/W3188); intercompany framework refresh; PFRS 16 adoption/maintenance
fields.Volume: ~205+ properties; intercompany lease to BuildRight Depot Inc. on every owned site

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "methodology" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Legal/Lease Admin create per-property intercompany lease" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-521 (ensure controlled execution — Landlord Leasing Operations & Tenant Management (PA-97.2).)
- operational: W3207 benchmarking and TP documentation; operational: lease-accounting policy and review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Transfer-pricing risk**: Non-arm's-length intercompany rent attracts BIR adjustment and penalties; mitigated by W3207 benchmarking and TP documentation
- **Mis-classification risk**: Wrong PFRS 16 lease classification distorts revenue/finance income; mitigated by lease-accounting policy and review
System Touchpoints: - Lease/contract module; transfer pricing (links to VS-72); tax (links to VS-79); GL/consolidation (links to VS-17)
Time Estimate: - 8–12 weeks initial framework; 1–2 weeks per new property schedule

steps.activity: Lease Admin/Tax (links to VS-79/VS-72) establish the intercompany lease framework: arm's-length rent per transfer-pricing rules (links to VS-72), base-rent methodology (per-sqm market rent benchmarked to comparable third-party leases — W3207), CAM pass-through, escalation formula, party roles (Property Mgmt Inc. as lessor; Depot Inc. as lessee); document arm's-length support per BIR transfer-pricing documentation (RR 02-2013)

Legal/Lease Admin create per-property intercompany lease (or master intercompany lease with schedules): premises description, term, rent, CAM, utilities, maintenance responsibilities, insurance (links to W3204), restoration/make-good, dispute resolution; classify lease under PFRS 16 for lessor accounting (operating vs finance lease)

Finance (links to VS-17.2/VS-72) book lessor lease and set up straight-line rent recognition (operating lease) or finance-lease receivable (finance lease); configure intercompany rent billing (W3195) and elimination on consolidation (links to VS-17.2)

fields.Participants: Leasing Mgr, Director, Facilities & Real Estate, Legal, Finance, Store Ops (links to VS-07), Tenant
fields.Trigger: Available leasable space (anchor, in-line, outlot/pad); third-party tenant inquiry
fields.Volume: ~1–3 third-party tenants per store/property; ~200–600 third-party agreements chain-wide (overlaps W177 concessionaire scope for in-store)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "Leasing Mgr source and qualify tenants for outlot/pad/anchor space" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-assign of "Negotiate commercial terms" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-521 (ensure controlled execution — Landlord Leasing Operations & Tenant Management (PA-97.2).)
- operational: credit screening and security deposits (links to VS-86); operational: clear use clause and audit (W3196)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tenant-credit risk**: Tenant insolvency creates vacancy and uncollected rent; mitigated by credit screening and security deposits (links to VS-86)
- **Use-clause creep risk**: Tenant drifts into competing uses; mitigated by clear use clause and audit (W3196)
System Touchpoints: - Lease origination/CMS; KYB (links to VS-86); permits (links to VS-22); billing (links to W3195); property/tenant master (links to VS-29)
Time Estimate: - 8–24 weeks per tenant from sourcing to commencement

steps.activity: Leasing Mgr source and qualify tenants for outlot/pad/anchor space: tenant mix strategy (banks, ATMs, food/beverage, courier drop-points, pharmacies — complementary, non-competing with BuildRight); tenant creditworthiness (links to VS-86 KYB/financial review), trade-mix fit, fit-out capability; align with Store Ops (links to VS-07) for site compatibility

Negotiate commercial terms: base rent (fixed + percentage rent), CAM/utilities recovery, term and options, tenant improvement allowance, co-tenancy/exclusivity clauses, use clause, assignment/subletting, insurance/indemnity (links to W3204); Legal drafts lease (links to VS-22 contract review)

Onboard tenant: lease execution, rent commencement, build-out coordination and permits (links to VS-22/VS-76), certificate of occupancy, rent deposit/security, insurance certificates, set up billing (W3195); integrate to property master (links to VS-29) and rent roll

fields.Participants: Property AR Mgr, Lease Admin, Finance (links to VS-16/VS-17), Facilities (links to VS-20.3/W3205)

workflows.name: Rent Billing, CAM Recovery & Tenant Receivables

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "generate monthly rent roll billing" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "post lessor revenue" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document dispute resolution" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-134 (ensure property income & LGU tax compliance (as owner).)
- operational: transparent CAM ledger and lease-defined recoveries; operational: deposits, dunning (links to VS-16)
Pain Points / Risks: - **CAM dispute risk**: Tenants challenge recoverable-expense classification and pro-rata share; mitigated by transparent CAM ledger and lease-defined recoveries
- **Rent-collection risk**: Third-party tenant delinquency; mitigated by deposits, dunning (links to VS-16.2), and default process (W3199)
System Touchpoints: - Lease/billing engine; e-invoicing/BIR (links to VS-79); AR (links to VS-16); GL/consolidation (links to VS-17); utility sub-meter (links to VS-20.3)

steps.activity: Lease Admin/AR generate monthly rent roll billing: base rent (per lease/escalation schedule W3197), CAM recovery (actual vs estimated — reconcile annually), utility recharges (sub-metered electricity/water per W1563/W701 where applicable), percentage rent (sales-based where applicable, requires tenant sales reporting); issue invoices (e-invoicing/BIR compliance links to VS-79)

Finance post lessor revenue (operating-lease income straight-lined per PFRS 16; intercompany rent eliminated on consolidation per VS-17.2); manage tenant receivables aging, dunning, and allocation (links to VS-16.2 AR/collections methodology); segregate intercompany from third-party for consolidation

Annually reconcile estimated vs actual CAM/utilities: compute each tenant's pro-rata share of recoverable operating expenses (excluding landlord-responsibility items), issue CAM reconciliation statement, true-up via credit/charge (mirrors BuildRight-as-tenant CAM reconciliation in VS-20.1 W1183 but from the landlord side); document dispute resolution

fields.Participants: Property Mgr, Facilities (links to VS-20.3/W3205), Leasing Mgr, Store Ops (links to VS-07), Tenant
fields.Trigger: Tenant request; scheduled service; relationship cycle

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-dispatch of "dispatch vendor or facilities team" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document and route opportunities to Leasing" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-inspect of "Property Mgr enforce lease compliance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-521 (ensure controlled execution — Landlord Leasing Operations & Tenant Management (PA-97.2).)
- operational: alteration-approval and inspection program; operational: SLA and relationship reviews
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lease-noncompliance risk**: Uncontrolled tenant alterations/safety violations create liability; mitigated by alteration-approval and inspection program
- **Tenant-experience risk**: Poor service drives non-renewal and vacancy (links to W3198); mitigated by SLA and relationship reviews
System Touchpoints: - CAFM/CMMS (links to VS-20.3); lease compliance/CMS; tenant CRM; insurance registry (links to W3204)
Time Estimate: - Per request + quarterly reviews; ongoing oversight

steps.activity: Property Mgr/Facilities manage tenant service requests: maintenance of landlord-provided systems (structural, roof, parking, shared utilities, common areas), triage by urgency and lease-responsibility split, dispatch vendor or facilities team (links to VS-20.3); track SLA and tenant satisfaction

Property Mgr conduct periodic tenant relationship reviews: occupancy experience, fit-out/alteration requests, sales performance (for percentage-rent tenants), expansion/downsizing needs, renewal intent (links to W3197); document and route opportunities to Leasing

Property Mgr enforce lease compliance: use clause, operating hours, signage, house rules, insurance certificates current (links to W3204), Alteration/fit-out approval; coordinate joint inspections; manage disputes before escalation to W3199

fields.Participants: Leasing Mgr, Property Mgr, Finance/Tax (links to VS-79/VS-72), Legal, Store Ops
fields.Trigger: Lease expiry approaching (12–18 months out); scheduled escalation; market-rent review clause

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "prepare renewal recommendation" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews and amends lease" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "accounting and billing" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-134 (ensure property income & LGU tax compliance (as owner).)
- operational: early engagement (12–18 months) and renewal incentives; operational: lease-admin calendar and automated billing
Pain Points / Risks: - **Renewal-loss risk**: Losing a key anchor/tenant disrupts mix and NOI; mitigated by early engagement (12–18 months) and renewal incentives
- **Escalation-error risk**: Missed escalations leak rent; mitigated by lease-admin calendar and automated billing
System Touchpoints: - Lease lifecycle/CMS; transfer pricing (links to VS-72); tax (links to VS-79); billing (W3195); GL (links to VS-17)

steps.activity: Leasing Mgr/Finance analyze renewal economics: current vs market rent (benchmark to W3207), tenant credit and performance, renewal vs reletting cost/benefit, capex requirements; for intercompany, refresh arm's-length benchmark (links to VS-72); prepare renewal recommendation

Negotiate and execute renewal: rent and escalation terms, TI for renewal, term/options, updated clauses (insurance W3204, regulatory compliance); apply scheduled escalations automatically; Legal reviews and amends lease

Finance update lease accounting and billing (W3195): revised straight-line schedule, new commencement/term, re-measurement under PFRS 16 if terms modified; update property master and portfolio analytics (W3208)

fields.Participants: Leasing Mgr, Marketing (links to VS-14), Property Mgr, Director, Facilities & Real Estate, Broker
fields.Trigger: Tenant notice of departure (W3199/exit); newly developed leasable space (W3188); persistent vacancy
fields.Volume: ~1–5% vacancy at any time across portfolio

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "prepare vacancy marketing" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate fit-out/permits for new tenant" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "Track vacancy KPIs" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-521 (ensure controlled execution — Landlord Leasing Operations & Tenant Management (PA-97.2).)
- operational: pre-emptive marketing before tenant exit and flexible interim uses; operational: deal-economics discipline
Pain Points / Risks: - **Downtime risk**: Extended vacancy erodes NOI; mitigated by pre-emptive marketing before tenant exit and flexible interim uses
- **Concession-creep risk**: Excessive TI/commissions erode net effective rent; mitigated by deal-economics discipline
System Touchpoints: - Marketing/CRM (links to VS-14); KYB (links to VS-86); lease origination (W3194); portfolio analytics (W3208)

steps.activity: Leasing Mgr/Marketing (links to VS-14) prepare vacancy marketing: space spec sheet, photos/render, demographics/traffic, asking rent, tenant-mix strategy, target tenant list; list with brokers and on commercial platforms
Leasing Mgr manage inquiries and tours: prospect qualification (links to VS-86 KYB), site tours, term sheets, negotiation; coordinate fit-out/permits for new tenant (links to W3194)
Track vacancy KPIs: physical vs economic vacancy, downtime (days vacant), leasing cost (TI + commission) per deal, concession cost; feed portfolio analytics (W3208) and capital plan (W3185)

fields.Participants: Property Mgr, Legal, Finance/AR (links to VS-16.2), Director, Facilities & Real Estate, Sheriff/LGU, Recovery (links to VS-21/VS-23)
fields.Trigger: Rent delinquency; lease breach; abandonment; insolvency

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "document all steps for evidentiary use" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate with LGU/sheriff for peaceful execution" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "Recovery and reletting" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-521 (ensure controlled execution — Landlord Leasing Operations & Tenant Management (PA-97.2).)
- operational: watertight lease, demand-letter discipline, and security deposits; operational: inventory-at-commencement, deposit, and restitution claims
Pain Points / Risks: - **Protracted-ejectment risk**: Philippine ejectment cases can take 6–18 months; mitigated by watertight lease, demand-letter discipline, and security deposits
- **Asset-recovery risk**: Tenant removes fixtures/damages premises; mitigated by inventory-at-commencement, deposit, and restitution claims
System Touchpoints: - AR/collections (links to VS-16.2); legal case management (links to VS-100); records/evidence (links to VS-88); tenant master (links to VS-29)

steps.activity: AR/Property Mgr detect default: rent aging (links to VS-16.2), breach (use/insurance/maintenance), abandonment indicators; issue demand letter and cure-period notice per lease and Philippine civil law; document all steps for evidentiary use

Legal pursue remedies per lease and law: ejectment filing (Regional Trial Court for forcible entry/unlawful detainer under Rules of Court), provisional remedies (preliminary attachment), apply security deposit to arrears, claim damages and unpaid rent through lease term or reletting; coordinate with LGU/sheriff for peaceful execution

Recovery and reletting: recover possession, secure and clean premises, assess damages vs deposit, pursue deficiency claim (links to VS-16.3/VS-21), relet space (W3198), update tenant and receivable records; capture lessons for tenant screening (W3194)

fields.Participants: Leasing Mgr, Property Development Mgr (links to W3188), Legal, Finance, Director, Facilities & Real Estate
fields.Trigger: Surplus land/outlot; ground-lease opportunity; pad development

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Leasing/Property Dev identify pad/outlot opportunities" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review mechanisms, reversion at term, tenant build obligations and approvals,…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitoring" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-521 (ensure controlled execution — Landlord Leasing Operations & Tenant Management (PA-97.2).)
- operational: maintenance covenants and reversion inspection; operational: use-clause/exclusivity protections
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reversion-condition risk**: Tenant-built improvements returned in poor condition at lease end; mitigated by maintenance covenants and reversion inspection
- **Cannibalization risk**: Pad tenant competes with BuildRight store; mitigated by use-clause/exclusivity protections
System Touchpoints: - Lease/CMS; project accounting (links to VS-40); billing (W3195); portfolio analytics (W3208)

steps.activity: Leasing/Property Dev identify pad/outlot opportunities: surplus land on owned sites, market demand (QSR, banks, fuel, pharmacies, logistics hubs), ground-lease vs out-right pad sale economics, BuildRight-store adjacency/traffic benefit; obtain investment approval

Legal/Leasing structure and execute: ground lease (long-term, tenant builds) vs BuildRight-built pad for lease (W3188 TI), rent reset/review mechanisms, reversion at term, tenant build obligations and approvals, exclusivity/co-tenancy; account for lessor ground lease under PFRS 16

Ongoing management: pad-tenant billing (W3195), CAM, compliance monitoring (W3196), renewal/escalation (W3197); portfolio reporting on outlot yield and contribution to overall property NOI (W3201/W3208)
